method: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from British Society for Rheumatology (Denton CP et al.), Rheumatology (Oxford) 63(11):2956 'The 2024 British Society for Rheumatology guideline for management of systemic sclerosis' (published 11 September 2024). Every claim is a paraphrase backed by anchors (scripts/anchor.py): verify.py --source re-finds each anchored span in a fresh copy of the source, checks the claim's numbers against it and rejects copying. LICENCE: CC BY-NC 4.0 (read at Europe PMC fullTextXML <license> element for PMC11534099). The source's words are NOT reproduced here.

claims.claim: **The gut is the organ most often involved in SSc**, and GI symptoms are among the most burdensome for patients, adults and children alike.
claims.locator: British Society for Rheumatology (Denton CP et al.), Rheumatology (Oxford) 63(11):2956, 'The 2024 British Society for Rheumatology guideline for management of systemic sclerosis', published 11 September 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11534099/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Reflux oesophagitis often responds to acid suppression, but dysmotility and anorectal disease with incontinence are much harder to treat.** Gastroenterology and, when needed, GI surgical input can transform outcomes.
claims.locator: British Society for Rheumatology (Denton CP et al.), Rheumatology (Oxford) 63(11):2956, 'The 2024 British Society for Rheumatology guideline for management of systemic sclerosis', published 11 September 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11534099/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Nutrition matters**: many people struggle to eat enough, and dietary changes can help both gut and general disease.
claims.locator: British Society for Rheumatology (Denton CP et al.), Rheumatology (Oxford) 63(11):2956, 'The 2024 British Society for Rheumatology guideline for management of systemic sclerosis', published 11 September 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11534099/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Optimise and check adherence to general and lifestyle measures** for oesophageal symptoms such as reflux. (1C, 99%)
claims.locator: British Society for Rheumatology (Denton CP et al.), Rheumatology (Oxford) 63(11):2956, 'The 2024 British Society for Rheumatology guideline for management of systemic sclerosis', published 11 September 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11534099/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Use a proton pump inhibitor and/or an H2-receptor antagonist for symptomatic reflux and dysphagia.** (1C, 99%)
claims.locator: British Society for Rheumatology (Denton CP et al.), Rheumatology (Oxford) 63(11):2956, 'The 2024 British Society for Rheumatology guideline for management of systemic sclerosis', published 11 September 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11534099/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Prokinetics (for example dopamine-antagonist promotility drugs) may be added** for dysphagia and reflux. (1C, 98%)
claims.locator: British Society for Rheumatology (Denton CP et al.), Rheumatology (Oxford) 63(11):2956, 'The 2024 British Society for Rheumatology guideline for management of systemic sclerosis', published 11 September 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11534099/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **If reflux is refractory**, investigate upper GI structure and motility and confirm acid reflux, for example with pH testing. (2C, 96%)
claims.locator: British Society for Rheumatology (Denton CP et al.), Rheumatology (Oxford) 63(11):2956, 'The 2024 British Society for Rheumatology guideline for management of systemic sclerosis', published 11 September 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11534099/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Barrett's metaplasia is common in SSc** and, with other risk factors, should prompt follow-up gastroscopy; a history of Barrett's oesophagus marks a high-risk case for follow-up cancer screening. (2C, 94%)
claims.locator: British Society for Rheumatology (Denton CP et al.), Rheumatology (Oxford) 63(11):2956, 'The 2024 British Society for Rheumatology guideline for management of systemic sclerosis', published 11 September 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11534099/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **In SSc lung disease, manage reflux as part of supportive care**; oesophageal involvement may limit eligibility for lung transplant.
claims.locator: British Society for Rheumatology (Denton CP et al.), Rheumatology (Oxford) 63(11):2956, 'The 2024 British Society for Rheumatology guideline for management of systemic sclerosis', published 11 September 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11534099/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **For symptomatic small intestinal bacterial overgrowth, give intermittent broad-spectrum oral antibiotics** (for example ciprofloxacin), possibly rotating agents; rifaximin is an option when refractory. (2B, 95%)
claims.locator: British Society for Rheumatology (Denton CP et al.), Rheumatology (Oxford) 63(11):2956, 'The 2024 British Society for Rheumatology guideline for management of systemic sclerosis', published 11 September 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11534099/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Stop a fluoroquinolone at the first sign of a serious adverse reaction**, such as tendon pain or inflammation.
claims.locator: British Society for Rheumatology (Denton CP et al.), Rheumatology (Oxford) 63(11):2956, 'The 2024 British Society for Rheumatology guideline for management of systemic sclerosis', published 11 September 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11534099/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Diarrhoea and constipation often alternate**: treat symptomatically with antidiarrhoeals (for example loperamide) or laxatives, after excluding non-SSc causes. (1C, 96%)
claims.locator: British Society for Rheumatology (Denton CP et al.), Rheumatology (Oxford) 63(11):2956, 'The 2024 British Society for Rheumatology guideline for management of systemic sclerosis', published 11 September 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11534099/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Pelvic floor physiotherapy with anorectal biofeedback** may help selected patients with incontinence. (2C, 91%)
claims.locator: British Society for Rheumatology (Denton CP et al.), Rheumatology (Oxford) 63(11):2956, 'The 2024 British Society for Rheumatology guideline for management of systemic sclerosis', published 11 September 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11534099/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Consider parenteral nutrition for severe weight loss or malnutrition (including high risk) that does not respond to enteral supplements.** (1B, 97%)
claims.locator: British Society for Rheumatology (Denton CP et al.), Rheumatology (Oxford) 63(11):2956, 'The 2024 British Society for Rheumatology guideline for management of systemic sclerosis', published 11 September 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11534099/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Children with juvenile SSc:** actively assess and monitor nutrition, growth and puberty, and manage faltering growth with tertiary paediatric gastroenterology and dietetic input. (1C, 99%)
claims.locator: British Society for Rheumatology (Denton CP et al.), Rheumatology (Oxford) 63(11):2956, 'The 2024 British Society for Rheumatology guideline for management of systemic sclerosis', published 11 September 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11534099/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Operate on GI complications only when essential and there is no alternative.** (1C, 97%)
claims.locator: British Society for Rheumatology (Denton CP et al.), Rheumatology (Oxford) 63(11):2956, 'The 2024 British Society for Rheumatology guideline for management of systemic sclerosis', published 11 September 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11534099/, retrieved 2026-09-23
